messages:
Priya Nair: Hey all — quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A. Posting compact answers to the common review/comp/promos questions we got. Please reply here if you need more detail or want us to escalate. :wave:

Alex Chen: Quick Q — the review email said 'effective April 1' but payroll runs mid-month. Which date should I expect on the paystub?

Priya Nair: Good question. Effective date = April 1 (that's the official promo/comp effective date). Payroll processes the change on the next scheduled payroll (usually Apr 15), so the first paycheck reflecting the change will be the mid-April run. We'll confirm exact payrun with Finance.

Samira Patel: If my manager is on leave during calibration (they're out 4/2–4/12), will my review still go through?

Priya Nair: Yes — reviews still proceed. If a manager is out, we pull in the backup reviewer (director or acting manager) plus recent peer feedback. If anyone has a manager out and wants us to flag it, DM me the manager + coverage name and we'll make sure it's in the packet. :+1:

Luis Gomez: How do we handle leveling exceptions for ICs who recently got an external offer and asked for an internal match earlier this year?

Maya Li: We won't automatically match external offers. During calibration we look at scope, impact, and consistency with banding. If it's a clear mismatch, managers can present evidence during calibration and request an exception; those require director + People Ops signoff. DM me if you want a quick consult.

people-ops-bot: Heads up — calibration packet submission deadline extended to 2024-04-05 17:00 PT. Please upload manager notes & evidence by then.

Priya Nair: Calendar invites were updated. If you didn't see the new deadline, check the shared calendar or ping @Rebecca.

Rebecca Ortiz: Also updated the review guidelines doc this morning — includes examples of impact statements and acceptable evidence. Link (internal): https://redwood.internal/hr/review-guidelines

Alex Chen: Any change to parental leave top-up this cycle? A teammate asked about extra months.

Priya Nair: No changes this cycle. We're actively researching expanded top-up pilots for next fiscal; we'll run a survey after the review window to gather feedback.

Samira Patel: Appeals — what's the window and what should be included?

Priya Nair: Appeals window is 30 days from comp/offer notification. Include manager notes, concrete examples of impact, and any missed evidence. Appeals reviewed by a small panel; expect a response within 14 business days.

Luis Gomez: Can managers pre-authorize budget for out-of-cycle promos for retention cases?

Maya Li: Out-of-cycle promotions require director + People Ops signoff and a budget note. For critical retention cases we can fast-track with an escalation to me + Finance; include clear retention risk and counteroffer details.

Priya Nair: TL;DR for the thread: effective date vs paydate clarified, managers-on-leave handled, appeals = 30 days, calibration deadline extended. If anything is unclear DM me or drop the manager+issue here and we'll prioritize.

Priya Nair: Quick timeline snippet for copy/paste into teams/dev docs:```
Effective date: 2024-04-01
Calibration packet deadline: 2024-04-05 17:00 PT
Payroll change visible on paycheck: 2024-04-15
Appeals window: 30 days from notification
```

Alex Chen: Thanks — that helps. :thumbsup:

Samira Patel: Appreciate it, Priya. Will DM about my manager coverage.

Priya Nair: Thanks everyone — we're keeping an FAQ doc updated in the HR folder. Will post once the payroll confirm comes back from Finance.
